name: EmailOctopus
summary: Email marketing for newsletters and small businesses, with a free plan for 2,500 subscribers and a Pro plan that removes branding.
best_for: newsletter publishers and small businesses that want a cheap, simple sender with a free tier and no trial clock
skip_if: you need advanced automations or a CRM in the same tool, or you want a tool we have tested on a paid plan ourselves
honest_knock: The free plan puts EmailOctopus branding on your emails and keeps reports for 30 days. The price grows with your list: the $9 entry figure covers up to 500 subscribers, and 2,500 subscribers cost $18 a month billed yearly. In our test (18 Nov 2026) mail went out from an EmailOctopus send address until a domain was verified. We have not paid for a plan, so deliverability and automations are untested by us.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro · per month billed yearly for up to 500 subscribers and 10,000 emails
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-18 on emailoctopus.com/pricing and its Markdown version, US dollars; earlier: read 2026-11-17) Starter: free, 2,500 subscribers, 10,000 emails a month, branded emails, reports for 30 days, 1 landing page, 1 form, 1 user. Pro: $10 a month, or $9 a month billed yearly ($108 a year, saves $12), for up to 500 subscribers and 10,000 emails a month; $20 a month, or $18 a month billed yearly ($216 a year), for 1,001 to 2,500 subscribers and 25,000 emails. The price rises with subscriber count. In euros the entry tier is 10 EUR a month or 9 EUR billed yearly. In our test (18 Nov 2026) the app called the free plan Starter and said it is limited to one form, but did not show the subscriber, email or report limits; without a verified domain it sent from an EmailOctopus send address because of DMARC, and a campaign could only be saved once the list had at least one contact. Nonprofits get 20% off for life. No free trial. We have not paid for a plan.

schema_offer.description: Pro, per month billed yearly for up to 500 subscribers and 10,000 emails ($108 a year; $10 billed monthly); $18 a month billed yearly at 1,001 to 2,500 subscribers; price rises with subscriber count; Starter is free for 2,500 subscribers. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-18.

free_plan_evidence: In our test (18 Nov 2026) the app called the free plan Starter and said it is limited to one form, but did not show the subscriber, email or report limits; without a verified domain it sent from an EmailOctopus send address because of DMARC, and a campaign could only be saved once the list had at least one contact.

compare_with.name: ActiveCampaign
compare_with.why: ActiveCampaign adds CRM and deep automation, while EmailOctopus stays a plain sender with low prices. Pick on whether you need journeys or just newsletters.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested EmailOctopus in our new free account (called Starter in the app): an inline sign-up form was ready in about 5 minutes and still shows Powered by EmailOctopus, a second form was refused (Your Starter plan is limited to one form), a campaign on the Announce template was made and previewed with nothing sent, and a welcome automation was made as a draft and not started, with no limit seen on Starter. Saving a campaign needed at least one contact, and a DMARC warning said that without a verified domain EmailOctopus sends from an address of its own. The Pro price matches the dossier ($9 a month billed yearly, $18 at 2,500 subscribers with 25,000 emails); the 10,000 emails apply only at 500 subscribers, and the Starter limits of the dossier are not visible in the app. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used a new EmailOctopus our account on the free plan, already signed in, with the interface in English. The free plan is called Starter in the app. The test started at about 11:20; the dashboard opened at once with no login step and no bot check, with the welcome line Welcome aboard! Start by adding your contacts. Setup and branding had been done before the test and nothing about an address or a person was filled in during it. The account has one single audience (Contacts, 0 subscribed contacts); the menu has Contacts, Grow, Campaigns, Automations, Reports and Brand, and no separate lists. The dossier name is EmailOctopus and the review is on MSS (emailoctopus-review); the handson folder and the review slug are the same. Core action 1, a sign-up form: Grow, Forms, Create a form. The styles are Inline, Pop-up, Hello bar and Slide-in, with five templates. An inline form on one template was chosen, renamed Test form, with the title Join the Garden Notes list and one line of text. Editing inline worked at once and the form was ready in about 5 minutes (11:25 to 11:30). The preview (Desktop and Mobile) shows Powered by EmailOctopus. The settings show the success message Thanks for subscribing!, an optional consent box and a hidden Google reCAPTCHA that is on by default. A second form was refused: Upgrade to add more forms, Your Starter plan is limited to one form. Core action 2, a campaign (nothing was sent): Campaigns first asks to add contacts. The setup did not go on without a contact (None of your subscribed contacts match this selection, and saving fell back to Untitled), so one placeholder contact on example.com was added (accepted, status Subscribed, no email went to it). Sender Test Co, subject Three herbs for your balcony. Saving showed Warning: verify your domain: because of a DMARC policy on the domain, mail from that address is unlikely to be delivered, so EmailOctopus would send from an address of its own sending domain instead; the choice was Continue, not Verify domain, and no domain was linked. The design step offers Branded templates (Announce, Birthday, Explore, Share, Update, Welcome), Inspirational, Start from scratch (Drag and drop or Code your own) and Past emails; Announce was chosen and takes the brand logo over. The editor blocks are Title, Text, Logo, Image, Video, Button, Social follow, Divider and Code. Typing the title and the text inline worked; a change to the small line Introducing you to: did not come through. The preview (Desktop and Mobile, Preview as Default with no personalisation) has a Send as test button that was NOT used. The footer holds the line that the reader subscribed and can unsubscribe, a placeholder return address of EmailOctopus itself, and the badge Sent with EmailOctopus. The review step shows All at once, More sending options marked Pro (gradual sending and smart timing, coming soon) and Send now or Schedule for later; Send now was NOT clicked. Core action 3, an automation: Automations, Create an automation, with six templates (Simple welcome, Birthday celebration, Check in, Re-engagement sequence, Landing page freebie, Monday motivation). Simple welcome was chosen and renamed Test welcome: trigger Contact added and one Send email step. The step types are email, wait, branch or condition, and action. It was left as a Draft and NOT started. A second automation was not refused at the start; whether a limit applies on Starter when activating was not tested, and none was seen. Other things seen on Starter: Segments and Tags were empty and usable with no lock shown; Fields hold only Email address, First name and Last name; Reports was empty (No reports yet). A help widget with a chat photo sits at the bottom right. Plans, read in the Upgrade to Pro pop-up (nothing clicked, no checkout): Pro in euros is 10 euro per month, or 9 euro per month billed yearly (Save 12 euro) for 500 subscribers and 10,000 emails per month; the currencies offered are AUD, CAD, EUR, GBP and USD; Pro in dollars is $9 per month billed yearly (Save $12) at the same tier; with 2,500 subscribers the pop-up shows $18 per month billed yearly (Save $24) and 25,000 emails per month. The yearly switch says Save 10%. The Pro list names removal of the EmailOctopus branding, unlimited forms and landing pages, unlimited automations with no practical limits, unlimited users with roles and permissions, gradual sending and smart timing (coming soon), up to 50 tags and fields, subscriber profile pages, reports available forever and priority help. Deviations from the dossier: the Pro price matches (from $9 a month billed yearly, saves $12, 10,000 emails at the entry tier, and the price rises with the number of subscribers: $18 at 2,500), but the 10,000 emails apply only at 500 subscribers. The dossier Starter limits (2,500 subscribers, 10,000 emails a month and reports for 30 days) are NOT shown in the app: not visible in the app. The one-form limit on Starter is shown and matches the Pro benefit of unlimited forms. The price fields of our pages are not touched. Checkout: NOT reached. The Upgrade to Pro button was not clicked, so no tax, total, card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: not applicable, no paid plan; the account was not deleted. Not tested: sending a campaign, a test email or starting an automation (on purpose); importing contacts, domain or DNS linking, integrations, landing pages, making segments or tags; complex journeys, a limit on a second automation, the subscriber and email limits of Starter, the length of report history; and the group of marketers who need complex automation. Clean up: the Test form, the Test campaign (draft), the Test welcome automation (draft) and the placeholder contact were deleted and checked empty. The account and the brand settings stay. No email was sent. The tab was closed.
exit_test.awkward: The free Starter plan allows one form only and keeps the EmailOctopus badge on the form and in the email footer. A campaign cannot be saved without at least one contact, and a sender address on a domain with a DMARC policy only gets a warning at the save step. The dossier limits of Starter (2,500 subscribers, 10,000 emails a month, 30 days of reports) are not shown anywhere in the app that was seen.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: Sending a campaign or a test email, and starting an automation, on purpose.
Importing contacts, linking a domain or DNS, integrations and landing pages.
A limit on a second automation, and the subscriber, email and report limits of Starter.
Checkout, a paid plan and cancelling.
The group of marketers who need complex automation.
Export and reimport.

Session and source-reading date: 18 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 11:20 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.

claim_checks.claim: Starter: free, 2,500 subscribers, 10,000 emails a month, branded emails, reports for 30 days
claim_checks.observed: The app calls the free plan Starter, says it is limited to one form and keeps the EmailOctopus badge on the form and in the email footer, but it shows no limit for subscribers or emails per month and no report history; those figures were not visible in the app.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier Starter limits against the screens of one new account; the app shows no figure for these three limits, and no limit was reached.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A reader cannot check from the app that Starter really allows 2,500 subscribers and 10,000 emails.

claim_checks.observed: The Upgrade to Pro pop-up showed $9 per month billed yearly with Save $12 at 500 subscribers and 10,000 emails per month, and in euros 10 euro per month or 9 euro billed yearly with Save 12 euro.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier entry price against the pop-up in dollars and euros at 500 subscribers; the pop-up was only read.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The entry price in the dossier is right.

claim_checks.claim: the price rises with subscriber count
claim_checks.observed: Typing 2500 in the subscribers field changed the price to $18 per month billed yearly (Save $24) and the emails to 25,000 per month.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier statement against one extra point on the price calculator; other sizes were not tried.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The bill grows with the list, so a growing list needs a new price check.

claim_checks.claim: 10,000 emails a month at the entry tier
claim_checks.observed: The 10,000 emails per month are shown only together with 500 subscribers; at 2,500 subscribers the pop-up shows 25,000 emails.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier entry tier against two points on the calculator; the entry tier itself is the 500 subscriber setting.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The 10,000 emails belong to a list of 500 people, not to every Pro buyer.

claim_checks.claim: Creators who outgrow the free branding
claim_checks.observed: The form preview shows Powered by EmailOctopus and the campaign footer shows Sent with EmailOctopus on Starter, and the Pro list names removal of the EmailOctopus branding.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier audience card against the form preview, the campaign footer and the Pro list; the Pro plan was not used to see the branding gone.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The free branding is real and Pro is the way to remove it.

claim_checks.claim: Pro ... adds unlimited users, landing pages and forms
claim_checks.observed: The pop-up Upgrade to add more forms says that the Starter plan is limited to one form and that Pro gives unlimited forms and landing pages; the Pro list also names unlimited users with roles and permissions.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier Pro list against the pop-up text; the Pro plan was not used, so unlimited was not tried.

claim_checks.claim: Unlimited automations with no practical limits
claim_checks.observed: A welcome automation was made from a template as a draft and not started; a second one was not refused at creation, and no limit on Starter was seen, but activating more than one was not tried.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: The Pro list line against a draft only; no automation was started, so no limit could show.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: It is unknown whether Starter blocks a second active automation.

claim_checks.observed: Only one simple welcome automation was made as a draft; complex journeys with branches were not built or run.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier audience card against a single draft with one email step; not part of the pain test.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about complex automation, where the dossier points to another tool.

claim_checks.observed: Saving a campaign with a sender address on a domain that has a DMARC policy showed a warning that mail from it is unlikely to be delivered, and that EmailOctopus would send from an address of its own sending domain; Continue was chosen and no domain was linked.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: A warning seen once with an address on a placeholder domain; the dossier makes no statement about it.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Without a verified domain the sender address of a campaign changes, which a newcomer sees only at the save step.

claim_checks.observed: The pop-up names the plan prices and the saving for yearly billing, but the Upgrade to Pro button was not clicked, so no tax, total or payment screen was seen.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was bought; the Upgrade to Pro pop-up was read without clicking its button
claim_checks.comparability: The pop-up amount against a checkout that was not reached; no stored cost rule was compared.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The final amount with tax is not confirmed.
